newsitem.title: USA: Panel backs $1 bln plan to ease Dallas traffic.
newsitem.headline: Panel backs $1 bln plan to ease Dallas traffic.

text.p: A panel of local officials on Friday proposed an ambitious 23-year, $1 billion plan to ease traffic congestion in the downtown Dallas freeway system, described as one of the nation's worst.

The proposed plan, which took 18 months to formulate and will now go to Dallas city council and other local bodies for approval, is a package of projects to be completed in phases through 2020 in order to spread the total cost.
No decision has yet been made on how to finance the project, but options may include turning the proposed roads into tollways and also issuing bonds.
The panel was made up of officials from the city of Dallas, Dallas County, the Texas Turnpike Authority and the state Department of Transportation as well as other local authorities.
The plan will require approval and support from nearly a dozen city, county, state and federal agencies, as well as citizens groups.

Dallas County Judge Lee Jackson, who chaired the panel and who will play a crucial role in getting the plan approved, said the project faced a long road ahead but that it had already won consensus support..

"I'm pleased with today's vote. A lot of agencies came together and a lot of work was done on the plan. This is just the first phase. We now have to determine how we are going to finance this," Jackson said.

Key parts of the plan known, as the "Trinity Parkway Corridor Major Transportation Investment Study", include a $430 million, 10-mile long, eight-lane Trinity Parkway, and a $431 million updating of the existing downtown "Mixmaster."
The Mixmaster, where traffic from Interstates 30 and 35 as well as five other highways converge, is blamed for much of the nightmarish traffic jams in the downtown area.
The Trinity Parkway, running along either sides of the Trinity River, would bypass the mixmaster congestion and provide a connection for Interstate 35 with two other highways.

The "Mixmaster" plan is a package of 200 invidual projects designed to create conditions for better use of existing lanes and to help prevent frequent lane changing. It would also provide a direct link between Inerstates 30 and 35.
Jackson said studies show that traffic is currently moving only at 10 miles per hour along these roads for as long as eight hours a day.
"If nothing is done, that will increase to more than 12 hours a day by the year 2010. That should give you an idea of the congestion we are taling about," he said.

Other recommendations in the $1 billion plan include building about 56 miles of trails and facilities for pedestrians and bicycle commuters, and using technological innovations to monitor traffic flows such as sensors and surveillance cameras.
